_source: Cavendish Coworking's doors. Ryan's brief, 2026-09-25: our Editorial and Operations meetings are open to the world as part of our commitment to transparency, they have been held in our Discord, and many people refuse to use Discord, so a shopfront on the street with doors that open the Proton Meet rooms. The Events room was added the same afternoon. EVERY TAGLINE, DESCRIPTION AND TIME IS WORD FOR WORD OFF OUR OWN EVENTS PAGE, https://stimpunks.org/events/, read in the Knowledge System mirror and against the live page on 2026-09-25; tools/make-coworking.py re-reads the mirror and refuses a line that is no longer on it. The door links are Ryan's, pasted in the brief. Each was opened on 2026-09-25 as far as Proton Meet's guest page and no further: it answered at meet.proton.me/guest/join/, asked for a name and no account, offered to go in without microphone or camera, and named the room exactly as `proton_name` says. Nobody joined a meeting to check. The doors are in the events page's own order, events before meetings, which is not ours to re-sort.

doors.name: Events
doors.tagline: The steady pulse beneath everything we do.
doors.said: Our recurring events are the heartbeat of Stimpunks: weekly, consistent, and always here.

slots.tagline: The radical act of showing up for each other.
Bring Your Muchness Down the Rabbit Hole
Expert lecturers. Community wisdom. Zero hierarchy.
Drop in. Space out. Belong here.
slots.said: Weekdays, 9AM Central — and spontaneously whenever someone feels like gathering

doors.name: Operations
doors.said: The Operations meeting is where the work of keeping Stimpunks running gets done. Each week we hold a task scrub — triage, prioritize, and move work forward together. If you want to understand how the organization operates or get involved in the doing, this is the meeting for you.

doors.name: Editorial
doors.tagline: Words, design, and everything we put into the world.
doors.said: The Editorial meeting is where we work on the Stimpunks website and print materials — writing, editing, and designing for publication. Whether you’re a writer, editor, designer, or someone who just cares deeply about how we communicate, join us.

_suites: The Hang Suites are Ryan's, written in his brief of 2026-09-25 and copied here as he gave them, with three changes: both lurking norms said 'camera and video off' and Ryan corrected them to 'camera and mic off' the same day; the Watering Hole's list of norms was headed 'Campfire Norms' in the brief, a slip, and is headed with its own room's name; and the opening line said how many rooms there are, which check-counts.py refuses, so it says 'rooms'. Each link was opened on 2026-09-25 as far as Proton Meet's guest page and no further, and named the room exactly as `proton_name` says. They are named for Cavendish Space's caves, campfires and watering holes, which are David Thornburg's, and make-coworking.py refuses the section if the room stops naming him. A suite has no times on purpose: they are drop-in rooms, and a suite with hours is a meeting and belongs with the doors.
suites_intro: Wanna just hang out or work on something together? We have rooms for that.

suites.name: Cave
suites.said: The Cave / Quiet Room is for quiet co-presence, ambient togetherness, and low-demand connection.
norms: It’s okay to text a hi to the room.

suites.name: Campfire
suites.said: The Campfire is for small groups and teams working on something together or watching/listening together.
norms: Mute when you’re not actively talking.
Quietly lurking with camera and mic off is perfectly fine and accepted.

rack._why: Ryan's brief, 2026-09-28: the Campfire gets the selection from the fire pit at Swaying Sweetgrass. The screen is that fire pit's own playlist, read out of data/sweetgrass.json by key; the cards are fires from it, each measured on its own watch page on the day: public, playable in an embed, not age-restricted, and its runtime. Their titles are the channel's and sell them for sleep and focus; the notes are ours and say only what is in them.
rack.rack_title: The fires, from the fire pit at Swaying Sweetgrass
rack.off: The whole playlist is off it until you put it back.

suites.name: Watering Hole
suites.said: The Watering Hole is for open, come-and-go, group Watercooler chat where random and off-topic are on-topic. This is a casual, drop-in space where people come together without any particular agenda.
norms: Mute when you’re not actively talking.
Quietly lurking with camera and mic off is perfectly fine and accepted.
Come-and-go as you please. If you need to drop out suddenly, no need to worry with goodbyes. We understand.

rack._why: Ryan's brief, 2026-09-28: the Watering Hole gets a selection from the Jungle Room, particularly the Namib Desert, the otters and the jellyfish. The cams are read out of data/jungle.json by id, never restated, so the two rooms cannot say two different things about one camera, and a cam that goes dark there goes dark here.
rack.rack_title: The cams: the desert, the otters and the jellies
rack.off: The desert is off it until you put it back.

access_note.title: A Note on Communication Access
access_note.said: We support multiple modes of participation including text chat, audio, and video — whatever works for your communication needs on a given day. You do not need to speak to belong here.

_rooms: Ryan's brief, 2026-09-28: Proton goes, and every door opens onto a room of its own with a call in it, through 8x8's Jitsi as a Service. A door with a `page` opens that room; `room` is the room's own name, `prefix` the class prefix its section of love.css dresses the generated parts in. Events, Operations and Editorial are public calls (PUBLIC_CALLS in netlify/cb/lib.mjs, which make-coworking.py reads); the suites are for people signed on to the CB. A door with no `page` yet still opens its Proton room, until its room is built.
